title: Voz pasiva y se impersonal: símbolos nacionales

sections.content: Se + verb states that something was done, widely and without a clear single author; ser + participle names who specifically did it when that detail matters. A story about how symbols were created often needs both. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Se adoptaron, en las nuevas repúblicas, banderas, himnos, escudos y ceremonias públicas.
items.english: Flags, anthems, coats of arms and public ceremonies were adopted in the new republics.

items.spanish: La bandera argentina fue diseñada por el general Manuel Belgrano en 1812.
items.english: The Argentine flag was designed by General Manuel Belgrano in 1812.

items.spanish: Se organizó un concurso público para elegir tanto la letra como la música del himno mexicano.
items.english: A public competition was organized to choose both the lyrics and the music of the Mexican anthem.

items.spanish: Estos símbolos fueron presentados, desde el principio, como si expresaran una esencia nacional profunda y preexistente.
items.english: These symbols were presented, from the start, as if they expressed a deep, pre-existing national essence.

sections.content: Notice se adoptaron doesn't name who adopted the symbols — governments, legislatures, specific people — while fue diseñada names Belgrano specifically. Reach for se when the collective adoption matters more than any one decision-maker; reach for ser + participle when a named individual is the whole point of the sentence.
